name: Five-tier product architecture (T1 KnowledgeOS / T2 KnowledgeOS Services / T3 Product PKS / T4 Business Product / T5 Running Software)
purpose: Layer the platform, its internal services, generated PKS instances, business products, and deployed evidence.
responsibility: Structural decomposition of what KnowledgeOS is and what it produces.
boundary: T2 is explicitly flagged by the source as 'the tier the recent work uncovered, and it is NOT PKS'.
non_responsibilities: Not repository roots — F0001 states the subsystems are INTERNAL and proposes no directory.
confidence: HIGH — stated verbatim in a table

name: Six internal subsystems (Governance, Capabilities, Validation, Runtime Integration, Operational Learning, PKS Generation)
purpose: The reusable platform's internal service layer (T2).
responsibility: Each carries its own evidence status — 3 operating, 1 at n=1, 1 governed-but-never-run, 1 responsibility-only.
boundary: INTERNAL. Promoting one to a repository root would encode an internal design decision as an ownership boundary.
non_responsibilities: Explicitly NOT repository roots; ES-005.2 independently forbids speculative directories.
conflicts: F0001 notes the source Addendum's diagram showed six while its own discipline table named three; F0001 resolves by marking each rather than dropping any.
change_note: F0010 §1 tests five of these six against the nine admissible-justification criteria and reclassifies them: Knowledge Validation = capability family (not domain), Runtime Integration = supporting subsystem + ACL, PKS Generation = merely an observation, Operational Learning = existing mechanism with 0 traversals.

name: Three-concern repository separation (PRODUCT docs/architecture/app/tests | ENGINEERING PLATFORM engineering/ | RUNTIME MOUNT .claude/)
purpose: Separate product knowledge from platform knowledge from runtime adapter.
responsibility: Ownership boundary by product, the axis F0010 calls 'stable'.
boundary: 'the mount never moves and is never the architecture'.
non_responsibilities: The runtime mount is explicitly NOT architecture.
source: F0009 O-6 (quoting ES-005.1); diagram in F0009 §7
confidence: HIGH — quoted verbatim from a cited standard
conflicts: F0005 and F0008 both record that ES-005.1 as written names PublicDigit and hard-codes .claude/ — a binding leak inside the governance layer itself.

name: Three architectural levels (Repository -> products | Product -> each product's architecture | Subsystem -> inside KnowledgeOS)
purpose: Keep product-ownership classification orthogonal to architectural-responsibility classification.
responsibility: Prevent an internal design decision being encoded as a repository-wide ownership boundary.
boundary: The two classifications 'are ORTHOGONAL and must not be collapsed'.

name: The five-arrow generation loop (KnowledgeOS -> PKS Generator -> Product PKS -> Business Product -> Operational Evidence -> back to KnowledgeOS)
purpose: Model how the platform is supposed to produce and learn from products.
responsibility: The loop-closing arrow is the platform's distinctive claim.
source: F0010 §5 (diagram with per-arrow evidence status); F0001 §5 lifecycle L-1..L-6
notes: Per-arrow evidence status is explicit and consistent across F0010 and F0001: 1 of 5 arrows EVIDENCED, the loop-closing arrow EMPTY, and one component (PKS Generator) that has never existed. This is the single most useful architectural finding in the batch.

name: Four platform-side bounded contexts (D-1 Engineering Governance, D-2 Engineering Method, D-3 Engineering Runtime, D-6a Evidence Protocol)
purpose: The semantic decomposition of KnowledgeOS as a platform, derived from ownership rather than from folders.
responsibility: Each owns its own language, lifecycle and invariants.
boundary: Platform-side only. D-6b (product evidence), D-7 instances and product domain knowledge are explicitly product-side.
non_responsibilities: Not folders - 'Folders are projections. No folder is proposed.'
confidence: MEDIUM - downgraded by F0024 (D-3 Strong->WEAK; D-2 Strong->MEDIUM)
conflicts: F0009 adds PD-3 as a fifth, scoring 6 of 9 and tying D-1 - so the count 'four, not eight' is itself already superseded within the same day.
note: Four candidates were DECLINED with the failed criterion cited in each case, 'so it cannot be re-proposed on preference'. That discipline is itself a reusable architectural practice.

name: The D-1 <-> D-2 authority relation
purpose: Determine whether Engineering Method is subordinate to Engineering Governance or its peer.
conflicts: Round39-MC was adopted by SPONSOR authority (ADR-M-012), not by the ARB - which is the evidence against subordination.
note: Called by its own source 'the model's most consequential open question', with the added constraint that NO DOCUMENT CAN SETTLE IT - it requires a governance act. For Step 2 this is a hard boundary of the theory seed: an unresolvable-by-reconstruction node.

name: Four progression kinds plus one non-progression
purpose: Explain why the repository has ten progression mechanisms rather than one lifecycle.
responsibility: Keep causally different kinds of change from being fused into a single lifecycle.
boundary: A governance-act progression can be GRANTED; an evidential progression can only be EARNED; provenance does not progress at all.
confidence: HIGH - derived from a 10-mechanism inventory answered against 7 questions each, with three prior canon refusals of fusion cited as corroboration
note: The most rigorously derived architectural object in 25 files: evidence-first, with the conclusion shown to EXTEND prior canon rather than found it.

name: The knowledge lifecycle with CHALLENGE and SATURATION stages
purpose: The observed (not designed) lifecycle of engineering knowledge in this repository.
responsibility: Describes how knowledge actually moves from discovery to platform.
conflicts: The terminal arrow (HARVEST -> PROMOTION -> PLATFORM) is marked 0 TRAVERSALS, which F0015 falsifies. See TH-0005.
note: INFERRED, NOT INVENTED - two stages (CHALLENGE, SATURATION) exist here that the commission's own example lifecycle omitted, and both are evidenced. An instance of the corpus correcting its own commission.

name: PD-3 - the Engineering Knowledge Platform domain
purpose: A governed domain with its own constitution, seven schemas, 18 enforced lint rules, a generated graph and a portal.
responsibility: Owns the knowledge substrate that F0020 had classified as a documentation layer.
boundary: Owner is a NAMED INDIVIDUAL, not the DA, ARB or sponsor - which is what makes it a domain rather than a substrate.
source: F0009 §3, recorded as a banner on F0020
confidence: HIGH - scores 6 of 9 criteria, tying D-1 as the most strongly evidenced domain
conflicts: Its admission means HA-0006's headline 'FOUR platform-side bounded contexts. Not eight.' was already wrong when written.
note: The corpus names its own error type: 'never asked WHO OWNED IT. That is a category error.' Ownership-blindness as a repeatable failure mode is itself a candidate theory object for Step 2.
